Rishi —

Thanks for the proposed text and the markup. We like the direction, but our legal team flagged two concerns:

1) "Provisional" invoices create complexity for our month-end close; our preference is clear line items that do not change post-month close unless a formal true-up is documented and dated.
2) The current Exhibit A/Order Schedule treats the Protective Band as a contractual rate cap, not an operational billing mechanism — our counsel wants stronger wording that prevents retroactive rate changes after final invoice issuance for a billing month.

We attached Arcadia_OrderSchedule_v3.pdf with inline notes. High-level ask from Arcadia: can Redwood provide a billing workflow paragraph that states any invoice adjustments will be documented as a separate true-up invoice dated in the quarter following the affected month, and that the original monthly invoice will retain a distinct reference code indicating it is "provisional" if it is subject to reconciliation.

Would Redwood accept the following compromise?
- Monthly invoice issued at provisional capped rate and labeled with a provisional reference code.
- No modification of the original monthly invoice PDF after issuance. Any reconciliation will be done via a separate true-up invoice in the subsequent quarter which references the provisional invoice(s) by code.

If you're ok with that, we can move to final legal redlines.

Thanks,
Tara

Team / Tara —

Legal read here. Ben and I reviewed both markups. The compromise Tara suggests is acceptable from Redwood's perspective with two clarifications we should add to the Order Schedule:

1) Include explicit definition of "provisional reference code" (example format: PROV-ARC-YYYYMM). This ensures both sides can tie provisional invoices to true-up line items without ambiguity.

2) Limit the window for adjustments to the subsequent quarter only (i.e., 90 days from month end). After that period, both parties waive rights to adjust that month's invoiced unit economics except for fraud or manifest error.

Suggested contract language (Order Schedule, Billing section):
"Monthly invoices that reflect provisional pricing under the Protective Band will be issued with a provisional reference code ("PROV-<Account>-<YYYYMM>"). Redwood will not alter the content of issued monthly invoices; any reconciliation required to effectuate contractual caps/floors will be captured in a separate true-up invoice issued within 90 days following the end of the month being reconciled. After 90 days, absent fraud or manifest clerical error, neither party may request retrospective adjustment to that month's invoiced amounts."

Operational note: Ben, please confirm that our billing ops can emit the provisional code format and the 90-day true-up window. If yes, I'll incorporate this language into the Redwood_ProtectiveBand_Markup.docx and send a tracked copy back to Arcadia.

-Laura
